> 莊子行於山中，見大木，枝葉盛茂，伐木者止其旁而不取也。問其故，曰：「無所可用。」

A great tree, in full leaf, and the woodcutter stops beside it and takes nothing. Why? "Nothing it can be used for."

The chapter opens with uselessness as survival, and then spends its length complicating that, because the same argument gets a man killed in the next paragraph.

## 不材: the price is quoted from outside

材: timber, usable material. 不材: no usable material.

The book's point is grammatical: the predicate "useful" is issued from outside. The tree did not fail a test; a test was applied to it. That is why 不材 is the chapter's 病根詞 — not because uselessness is bad, but because the whole sentence belongs to someone else.

## 訾 and the only safe starting point

訾: to slander, to disparage. 無譽無訾 — no praise, no blame.

The chapter puts both at the start, and the pairing is deliberate. Praise is included in what must be dropped, because praise installs the same machine as blame, with better manners.

## 一龍一蛇 is not "flexible"

龍出而蛇伏 — the dragon comes out, the snake lies low: extend and withdraw with the time.

The next clause blocks the usual reading: 與時俱化，而無肯專為 — change with the time, and be unwilling to be fixed as any one thing. It is not the diplomat's skill of adapting. 專為 is refused: no specialization into a self.

## 以和為量

量: the measuring vessel, the standard.

Take 和 as the measure — not 利, not 名.

This is the one place where the book's central distinction becomes an operational instruction. 合 is the manufactured join, the standard issued and enforced. 和 is each thing getting its place without harm. Measure by the second, and most of the first becomes visible as what it is.

## 物物而不物於物

First 物 is a verb: to treat as a thing, to wield. Second 物 is a noun: the external.

Use things; do not be used by things.

This is the chapter's 總綱, and its precision is easy to lose in the idiom it became. It does not say "don't care about things." It says: keep the verb.

## 刳形去皮: the word that matters is 皮

刳: to hollow out. 皮: skin, the outer layer.

魯侯's 皮 is 魯國 — the thing he cannot put down. Yours is whatever you would not survive losing.

That single word is the key to the chapter: the 皮 is not a vice, it is an identity that has become load-bearing.

## 建德之國

The fabled country's three marks: 知作而不知藏, they work and do not hoard; 與而不求其報, they give and do not ask for return; 不知義之所適，不知禮之所將, they do not know where rightness goes or where ritual leads.

Read carefully: not immoral. Virtue that has not become an item — 德不成條目.

## 虛船: the argument that does not happen

A boat with no one in it bumps yours, and even a person with the smallest temper does not get angry. 雖有惼心之人不怒 — 惼 reads 褊: narrow, petty.

Let a person be in it, and the shouting begins.

The lesson is not "be nice." It is that the anger is not about the collision. It is about the presence. Make yourself 虛己 — empty of that presence — and the collision has nothing to argue with.

## 意怠: the bird named Lazy

A bird of the chapter's own invention, and its name is 怠 — slack, idle.

翂翂翐翐, it flies low and slowly, 迫脅而棲, it roosts squeezed in among the flock. Not because it is weak: because it does not lead and does not trail, and is therefore not picked out.

## The test

Name the 皮 you are carrying — the one identity whose loss you could not absorb. Then ask the 虛船 question: when you collide with someone, is what they are angry at the collision, or your presence in the boat? And the 和 question: are you measuring this by 和, or by a score someone else issued?
